p: it came to pass: The law of the very sabbath ought not to hinder the offices of charity.

one of the chief Pharisees to: Either one of the elders, whom they called the sanhedrin, or one of the chiefs of the synagogue: for all the Pharisees were not chief men of the synagogue Joh 7:48; for this word Pharisee was the name of a sect, though it appears by viewing the whole history of the matter that the Pharisees had much authority.
And he put forth a parable: The reward of pride is dishonour, and the reward of true modesty is glory.

Then said he also to him: Against those who spend their goods either for the glory of man or for hope of recompence, whereas Christian charity considers only the glory of God, and the profit of our neighbour.
And they all with: For the most part even those to whom God has revealed himself are so mad, that any help which they have received of God they willingly turn into obstructions and hindrances.

one consent began to make excuse: On purpose, and a thing agreed upon before: for though they give different reasons why they cannot come, yet all of them agree in this, that they have their excuses so that they may not come to supper.
streets and lanes of the city: Wide and broad areas.

And there went great multitudes with: Even those affections which are in themselves worthy of praise and commendation must be controlled and kept in order, so that godliness may have the upper hand and have preeminence.
hate not his father: If anything stands between God and him, as Theophylact says: and therefore these words are spoken in a comparative way, and not by themselves.
And whosoever doth not bear his: The true followers of Christ must at once build and fight, and therefore be ready and prepared to endure all types of miseries.
sitteth not down first: At home, and calculates all his costs before he begins the work.
Salt is good: The disciples of Christ must be wise, both for themselves and for others: otherwise they become the most foolish of all.
